title: Mail: send a note, receive cards (/hub/notes/<n>/send, /hub/mail)
what:
src/mail/{mod.rs, send.rs, recv.rs}.
Send: POST /hub/notes/<n>/send {node, mesh?, hold?}
- Re-read the file; check the 64 KiB cap (413 with no spawn).
- node must be 'self' or a verified node from mesh::nodes; mesh, when given, must be one of that node's meshes.
- hold with self gives 400 'hold needs another node' with no spawn.
- Run R2a MailSend: to=<node>/minerva (self/minerva for self), from=Minerva, subject = the title on one line.
- 202 {msgid, disposition, delivery}.
- A data.reason (unknown-node, unpaired-node) becomes a sentence with 409. aoide's multi-mesh refusal becomes 409 {why, meshes}, so the page can ask which mesh.
- Append to <home>/mail/sent.jsonl {ts, origin:'operator', from:'minerva', note, sha256, to, mesh?, msgid, disposition}.
GET /hub/mail/nodes -> [{name, verified, self, meshes}], with 'this machine' first.
Receive: mail::start runs a task. Only while a page polled /hub/mail in the last 60 s, every 5 s:
- stat <aoide-home>/state/mail/base.jsonl (mtime, len); no aoide call while it is unchanged
- on a change, run MailRead (AOIDE_SESSION_ID=minerva-perch)
- letters are decoded as AOIDE-LETTER/1 when they parse, raw text otherwise; header fields are clamped to their grammars; the sender mailbox (minerva | minerva-agent | other) is kept for the card
- letters go to <home>/mail/received.jsonl (append-only, deduped by msgid, text ≤ 64 KiB) and cards.json (state new -> placed{chat} -> dismissed)
- receipts whose text equals a sent msgid mark that row delivered
- otherwise status comes from `mail outbox --json` (cached 60 s)
- once at start: --reread (cap 4 MiB) recovers cards lost between aoide advancing the cursor and the perch writing (`mail export` is read-only but returns Markdown threads across all mailboxes with no receipts, so it is not used)
Routes:
- GET /hub/mail -> {available, received:[card], sent:[row]}
- POST /hub/mail/<msgid>/place {chat} (64-hex msgid; chat passes id_ok and is known), /dismiss, /save (notes::create)
Nothing ever posts a card to a door. Cards land in the notes tab (a planner call, formerly D8).
tests:
tests/mail.rs with fake_aoide:
- Send:
  - the send argv is exact, with --from=minerva
  - 64 KiB + 1 gets 413 with no spawn; a subject with a newline gets 400 with no spawn; hold with self gets 400 with no spawn
  - unknown and unpaired nodes give sentences; the multi-mesh refusal gives 409 with meshes, and a resend with mesh passes --mesh
- Receive:
  - the stat gate: unchanged base.jsonl makes zero calls; a touch makes exactly one read
  - the reconcile dedups
  - a receipt marks delivered
  - hostile text (HTML, </script>, ANSI, broken AOIDE-LETTER) comes back as JSON strings
  - a minerva-agent sender is kept on the card
- Cards and files:
  - place needs a known chat
  - fake_eidolon logs no `say` for any card
  - sent.jsonl is 0600
live_check: fake perch on PORT=48118 with fake_aoide: send to self, poll, the card shows, place it.
risk:
- Note text sits in argv while aoide runs (visible in /proc), hence the 64 KiB cap.
- A self-send rings aoided, and its petname fallback could nudge a conducted session named `minerva`.
- Every mail read takes a flock; the runner's timeout covers a held lock.
- Held letters leave only when the receiving node polls. A Minerva perch never runs `mail poll`.
notes: M2 fix round (base e08e42d, branch worktree-agent-aba970ccc3baacf9f): the review's findings R1-R11, S1-S6 and V1-V2 are in M2-fix.md. This list records what changed against the text above; where it differs, this list wins.

D1 (spec drift): a newline in the subject cannot arrive over HTTP, because the note's title is its first line. The 'subject with a newline gets 400' line under tests never applies. The behaviour is a silent clean, as built: the subject is one printable line whatever the note starts with (tests/mail.rs a_subject_is_one_printable_line_whatever_the_note_starts_with). The inventory's 'newline -> 400' is corrected.
D2 (spec drift): the outbox refresh runs before the base.jsonl stat gate, so the rule is one outbox call a minute while a row waits (mail_ttl_ms), not 'cached 60 s' behind the stat gate.

Send answers in the --subject shape, which the perch always sends. Observed on aoide 0.0.26 (aoide-probe r-send-B): data.accepted is a count of accepted recipients; the one recipient is data.recipients[0], with accepted (bool), address, delivery, error, msgid, ring, role and status. The row's msgid, status, delivery and error come from recipients[0]; send.rs:366 treats recipients[0].accepted false as a refusal. aoide's 'disposition' key is not in that shape and is read nowhere. row.disposition in sent.jsonl is the perch's own copy of the recipient's status word, and recv.rs reads that copy (recv.rs:497, 519: the reads in current() and waiting() at 74ae824; at fbff34b they are the same lines). The 202 answer still names disposition, for that same perch copy (send.rs:7). The earlier '202 {msgid, disposition, delivery}' line is superseded by send.rs:7.

Receive: a plain read that fails or is too big re-arms a --reread after 30 s. A reread too big to print raises a permanent notice and is not re-armed. A reread that fails for another reason is retried after 60 s. Caps: plain read 4 MiB, reread 16 MiB, schema 512 KiB, mail send 45 s (formula in perch/src/mail/README.md).

V1 (narrowed): the aoide schema gate covers mail only. Its list includes mesh --json, because the mail send's node check reads it. The mesh view reads only version(), so a schema without the mesh command does not refuse mesh yet. The mesh gate (mesh/mod.rs:216-217 version_of, and mesh_of) belongs to the mesh owner, and tests/mesh.rs is outside M2's grant.
ratified 2026-10-08: grant perch/tests/mesh.rs as changed in bce45f6 (the wrapper and the `schema` argv), because V1 needs it. No further mesh.rs edit.

ratified 2026-10-08: V1 is narrowed to mail. The mesh half (mesh/mod.rs version_of and mesh_of calling schema_check, and the stale --version references in mesh/mod.rs and mesh/README.md) is a follow-up for the mesh owner after R2c and M2 are both on master. aoide/README.md says so where it claims a refusal turns mesh off.

ratified 2026-10-08: S2. `disposition` in SentRow is the perch's own key, written and read only by the perch; it is not aoide's field, and it is kept. One recipient per send, so recipients[0].accepted is the whole send's answer, and it is kept. mail/README.md says both.
